issue.title: Continuation agents lose opened-repo commit obligations, stranding external-repo edits after a monitor handoff

task_type_fields.impact:
Silent loss of verified work, plus closed beads claiming work that is not on any
branch. Every multi-turn agent that edits a repo opened with `sase repo open` is
exposed; cross-repo epic phases that pin sase-core and edit sase are the usual case.
The land agent had to discover the loss, rescue the diff from another workspace before
that workspace was reused, and send the work back through a new tale.
task_type_fields.location: SASE host finalizer: opened-repo obligation discovery for continuation agents (sase repo log attribution vs finalizer_baseline opened_repo scope)
task_type_fields.repro:
Observed on athena, 2026-10-28 (times EDT), discovered by lander bob-cli-df.2.1.4.3.3.land:

1. Phase agent `bob-cli-df.2.1.4.3.3.2` opened two external repos with `sase repo open`
   (`gh:sase-org/sase-core` and `sase`) at 08:09, and edited the opened `sase` checkout
   (core pin bump plus quarantine path fixes and tests: 4 files, +220/-1).
2. A monitored command handed the turn to continuation agent `bob-cli-df.2.1.4.3.3.2--1`
   (run 20261028085932). It finished the work, recorded notes, and closed the phase bead
   at 09:09.
3. The continuation's `finalizer_baseline.json` lists both opened repos (scope
   `opened_repo`, sase head 49ebcc5eba). But its `final_context.json` has
   `obligations: []` and `repository_evidence: []`, and `final_context_host.json` has
   `repositories: []`. The commit finalizer reported `success`, but
   `commit_results.json` holds only three beads-sidecar commits.
4. `sase repo log --agent bob-cli-df.2.1.4.3.3.2--1` shows zero open events. All opens
   are attributed to the predecessor agent name, so the continuation never received the
   opened-repo obligation.
5. Result: the closed phase claims work that is not on any branch. sase origin/master
   still pins sase-core 00fe29d5. The diff survived only as dirty files in the released
   workspace's external checkout, and a new agent was already STARTING in that workspace
   at 09:18.

Evidence: `file:explicit:e79819a22e42975e194405f7` (finalizer context, baseline, result,
and commit results), `file:explicit:ab5d6c3294bc3abbcfb7bf7b` (the stranded diff).

To reproduce: open an external repo with `sase repo open` in a SASE agent, edit it, end
the turn through a `/sase_monitor` handoff, and let the continuation agent finish and
declare. The continuation's final context omits the opened repo, and the edits are left
uncommitted.

issue.creation_reason: A continuation agent closed a phase bead while its predecessor's edits in an opened external repo were never committed, because the finalizer saw no opened-repo obligation. This is a SASE host defect, separate from the artifact-link epic that exposed it.

payload.description: Adjacent finalization defect: closed phase claims work not on master, different root cause (failed reset vs missing opened-repo obligation)
Phase whose opened-repo sase edits were stranded by the continuation finalizer

payload.entry: B4 outer-land reviewed the proposing nested land audit df.2.1.4.3.3 #1 and this typed repro. The stranded quarantine diff is now actually committed as SASE d0358b874f and integrated at 9a38ff35b1, so B4 implementation recovery is complete. The underlying continuation obligation-discovery defect remains this independent task; no new reproduction or duplicate task. The remaining B4 tale must reopen external repos on each continuation before finalization.
